# fortiappseccloud_waf_xml_protection_policy

Configures XML protection policy for one FortiAppSec Cloud application using the static app endpoint `/waf/apps/{ep_id}/xml_protection_policy`. Set `template = false` and provide `configs` to manage settings directly. Set `template = true` and omit `configs` to inherit this module from the application's attached WAF template.

Declare only one `fortiappseccloud_waf_xml_protection_policy` resource for an application endpoint. Template-level settings are managed by `fortiappseccloud_waf_template_xml_protection_policy`.

## Example Usage

```hcl
resource "fortiappseccloud_waf_xml_protection_policy" "example" {
  ep_id    = fortiappseccloud_waf_app.example.ep_id
  template = false

  configs {
    status = true
    action = "alert_deny"
    # file_list is omitted because creating a schema entry requires real file
    # content, which this generic module resource intentionally does not upload.
  }
}
```

## Configuration Notes

- `file_list` references XML-schema files already present in FortiAppSec Cloud. Omit that block when no uploaded schema exists; this resource does not upload schema files.

## Argument Reference

- `ep_id` (Required, Forces replacement) — Application endpoint ID. Import uses this exact value and it must contain a non-whitespace character.
- `template` (Required) — Whether effective configuration is inherited from the attached template.
- `configs` (Block) — Required when `template = false` and forbidden when `template = true`. State keeps this block null when template inheritance is enabled.
  - `action` (Optional, Computed) — Sets Action. One of `alert`, `alert_deny`, `deny_no_log`. Omission preserves the current value.
  - `bucket` (Optional, Computed) — Sets Bucket. Omission preserves the current value.
  - `prefix` (Optional, Computed) — Sets Prefix. Omission preserves the current value.
  - `status` (Optional, Computed) — Enables or disables XML protection policy. Omission preserves the current value.
  - Collection ownership — Each block below contains ordered `item` blocks. Omitting a collection block preserves the complete raw remote array and keeps the block null in state. A present empty block sends `[]`. A present block with items replaces the complete array in Terraform order.
    - `file_list` (Optional Block, at most 10 items) — Owns the ordered `file_list.item` blocks.
      - `file_list.item.entity_check` (Required) — Entity check.
      - `file_list.item.filename` (Required, maximum 58 UTF-8 characters) — Filename.
      - `file_list.item.limit_check` (Required) — Limit check.
      - `file_list.item.md5` (Optional, Computed) — Md5.
      - `file_list.item.name` (Required, maximum 32 UTF-8 characters) — Rule name.
      - `file_list.item.schema_valid` (Required) — Schema valid.
      - `file_list.item.url` (Required) — Request URL.

The wire-only `idx` field is never exposed. The provider regenerates sequential one-based indices independently for each list, validates imported or owned response indices, and sorts state by `idx`. Unknown nested item keys fail closed for owned and imported arrays; omitted top-level collection wrappers remain opaque and are preserved unchanged.


## Import

Import using the application `ep_id`:

```shell
terraform import fortiappseccloud_waf_xml_protection_policy.example application-endpoint-id
```

The first read after import hydrates all ownership wrappers when `template = false`.

## Destroy Behavior
Destroy performs a fresh GET, preserves the complete response, sets `template=false` and `configs.status=false`, sends the complete PUT, and verifies the normalized GET response before Terraform removes the resource from state.
